_comment: Scripted model replies for LLM_PROVIDER=fake (tutor_api/llm/fake.py): the browser end-to-end flows and the local compose stack. Every prompt gets the same three-block circuit (a 300 Hz sine, an RC low-pass whose first draft has a wrong pin, a follower); a word in the prompt picks a variant: e2e-cancel and e2e-reload hold the filter's composer, e2e-retry fails the planner once, e2e-unsupported asks for what no template builds. Ask: e2e-ask answers about the RC filter with an experiment (R1 to 100k), e2e-ask-fail is a model outage, e2e-ask-slow holds its answer 30 s; any other question gets a note that this is the scripted tutor.

uncovered: a microcontroller that reads the temperature

blocks.title: Test signal
blocks.purpose: V1 makes a 300 Hz sine wave to test the filter with.

blocks.title: Low-pass filter
blocks.purpose: R1 and C1 let low frequencies through and send high ones to ground.

blocks.title: Output buffer
blocks.purpose: U1 copies the filtered signal so a load cannot change the corner frequency.

rules.reply: This circuit filters a test signal. A sine source drives an RC low-pass filter, which passes slow signals and shunts fast ones to ground. An op-amp follower then buffers the result.

[R1] and [C1] set the corner of [block:b2]: fc = 1/(2π·R·C). A larger [R1] charges [C1] more slowly, so the corner moves down. [R9] is not in this circuit.

```try
{"ops": [{"op": "part.set_param", "body": {"refdes": "R1", "key": "resistance", "value": "100k"}}], "predict": "the cutoff drops well below 2 kHz"}
```
This is the scripted tutor (LLM_PROVIDER=fake): every question gets this same answer. Set a real provider in .env to have your questions answered.
